speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Aisha, thanks for making the time. Is the connection okay?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, it's fine. I'm at home today, it's a remote day.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. So this is just about your grocery orders, nothing to prepare.

speaker: interviewee
text: Good, because I didn't.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: It's just me. I'm a management consultant, I travel a lot, so honestly my fridge is mostly sparkling water and condiments. I shop when I'm in town, usually the small shop under my office.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: A colleague mentioned it in a meeting, he was ordering lunch stuff with it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Walk me through your last order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: I downloaded it, made an account, filled a basket really fast. Fruit, yogurt, frozen dumplings, coffee, the essentials. Then I went to pay.

speaker: interviewer
text: And was anything confusing?

speaker: interviewee
text: Well, at checkout it logged me out, right when I pressed pay, and I had to log in again and the basket was half empty. So I did it again. Twenty minutes, roughly.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Only that once, really. It was the week before a big client deadline, I was at my desk from seven till midnight, I genuinely could not leave the flat. When the project shipped I went straight back to grabbing things at lunch from the little shop under the office.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: The coffee. I wanted beans and I got ground. That one I minded a bit, I have a grinder for a reason.

speaker: interviewer
text: When did you find out about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: When I opened the bag. There was a notification, I think, but I was on a call. I don't read anything during calls.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: I don't, really. I look in the fridge and I see what's missing. Usually everything.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I picked the earliest one the next morning, eight to ten, before my first call.

speaker: interviewer
text: And did it fit your day okay?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, it came at eight thirty. Perfect, actually. I was in my pyjamas.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: In theory I'd pay, money isn't really the issue. But I'm away half the month. I'd forget to cancel it and resent it.

speaker: interviewer
text: So would 9.99 a month feel like too much?

speaker: interviewee
text: For me it's not the price, it's that I'm never home. If I were here every week, sure, ten is fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, why not. To people who work from home. It's handy.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What did you like the most?

speaker: interviewee
text: That it was fast. I ordered at eleven at night and had food at eight thirty.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The app itself feels a bit clunky. Too many screens before you can pay.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted. Great. Have you looked at the recipes section?

speaker: interviewee
text: There's a recipes section? No, I didn't see that.

speaker: interviewer
text: It's quite new. Great. Did you use your phone or a laptop for the order?

speaker: interviewee
text: The laptop, because I was at my desk anyway.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I think that's all. It was fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: Thank you so much, Aisha, this was really useful.

speaker: interviewee
text: Of course. Good luck.
